Hi Kavitha,
Short update on the image module, since I was stuck yesterday.
The imaging library we need would not install on my laptop. I spent three hours on it: different versions, clearing caches, reading forums. Every fix led to a new error. Around six I realised I was no longer working on the module at all, only fighting my laptop.
So I stopped and set a smaller goal: get a clean environment where the library works, even if it's not my machine. I set up a container with the right system packages. That took forty minutes. The library installed on the first try.
This morning I went back to the actual task, and the resize function now passes all twelve tests.
I've written the setup steps in our wiki so nobody else loses three hours.
Sharmila

Tushar, you look like I did last month, so sit for a minute. Your Madhav bhaiya has a story.
I needed one database driver for the payments feature. It wouldn't install. I tried every version, every forum answer. By Thursday evening I'd lost a day and a half and I was angry at my laptop, at the driver, at myself.
Then my team lead asked me one question: "Is your goal to install this driver, or to ship the feature?"
That flipped something. I stepped back and made a new small goal: a clean box where the driver works. I built a container, installed the driver there in twenty minutes, and ran my code inside it.
Friday I was back on the payments feature itself. So when you hit a wall, don't keep head-butting it. Make a side road, then come back.

qa.q: How long did it take Madhav to install the driver inside the container?
qa.a: Madhav installed it there in twenty minutes.

qa.q: How was Madhav feeling by Thursday evening?
qa.a: Madhav was angry and frustrated, at the laptop, the driver and at himself, after losing a day and a half.

qa.q: What other approach could help Tushar if a container is not possible?
qa.a: Tushar could ask a senior for a machine or setup where the tool already works, since the goal is the feature, not the install.

qa.q: How might the team lead have seen Madhav's day and a half of struggle?
qa.a: The team lead probably saw Madhav stuck on the wrong goal and chose one question to redirect him rather than giving the answer.
